articles.title: Lanterns Season 1, Episode 4 Review & Recap: "The Weenie"
articles.summary: Lanterns stumbles a bit in Episode 4 as it fails to take full advantage of some key DC characters, but the series’ core strengths remain. Read our full review.
body: Warning: This review contains full spoilers for Lanterns Season 1, Episode 4!

Lanterns sure left us hanging these past couple of weeks, ending Episode 2 with the debut of Ulrich Thomsen’s Sinestro and then pivoting away to tell a flashback storyline in Episode 3 ( a great flashback storyline, but a flashback all the same). Only now in Episode 4 do we see the full reunion between Sinestro and his former protege. It’s a definite high point of the episode, albeit an all too brief one.

I feel similarly about the other key GL villain introduced in Episode 4, Jason Manuel Olazábal’s Hector Hammond. We basically get one good, solid sequence out of Hector and that’s it. The standoff between Hector and Hal/John (Aaron Pierre) is tense and stressful in the best way, but it’s also over very quickly. At that point, we learn that Hector is really just Hector Gutiérrez, another fakeout used by the Manhunter to throw our heroes off their scent. And unlike Sinestro, there’s not even any prior history between Hal and Hector in this universe. This is a major DC villain who’s being effectively wasted as a one-off misdirection.
points: Lanterns stumbles a bit in Episode 4 as it fails to take full advantage of some key DC characters, but the series’ core strengths remain.

articles.title: Exodus Ending and Character Fates Change Based on Your Choices
articles.summary: Any time you look at or talk about Exodus, the upcoming space opera RPG from Archetype Entertainment, the Mass Effect comparisons start flying at light speed. I mean, Exodus narrative director Drew Karpyshyn played a major role as a writer and lead at BioWare to shape the stories of its biggest…
body: The parallels don't end with the Paladin/Immortal morality system or the romance and relationship dynamics that are going to drive the story, either. He hinted at how the decisions you make can impact Exodus' ending. Of course, that's not exclusive to BioWare games by any stretch, but when the Mass Effect 2's suicide mission is regarded as a series pinnacle, no one would blame to draw a quick comparison.

When I asked about the relationship systems in Exodus, Karpyshyn emphasized wanting to make them feel real and said it's about, "[M]aking their relationship with you grow, allowing it to evolve from the choices you've made, and realizing that the choices you make are going to bring some companions closer to you, but maybe push some companions farther away."

He took it one step further, and told me, "Without spoiling too much, we definitely want to have it impact how their storylines go." Then he took it another step further and concluded, "Depending on choices you make, by the end of the game, you might not have every companion with you that you started with. That's about all I can say!"
points: Any time you look at or talk about Exodus, the upcoming space opera RPG from Archetype Entertainment, the Mass Effect comparisons start flying at light speed.

articles.title: 7 Huge Differences Between Christopher Nolan's 'Interstellar' and Steven Spielberg's Original Script
articles.summary: But before Christopher Nolan signed on as the director of Interstellar, the director was none other than Steven Spielberg, who developed the story with Nolan’s screenwriter brother, Jonathan Nolan.
body: More than six weeks after its premiere, Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey is still going strong at the box office. Recently, it surpassed Deadpool & Wolverine to become the highest-grossing R-rated film of all time. As such, the celebration of Nolan’s entire filmography continues, including his 2014 sci-fi epic, Interstellar, which is about a team of astronauts traveling into deep space to find a new home for humans before the Earth becomes uninhabitable.

The script of Spielberg’s version of the film is accessible online, though. If you read it, it's clear that we would have gotten a much different movie. Here are the seven biggest differences between the Interstellar we got from Christopher Nolan and the version we almost got from Steven Spielberg.

In Christopher Nolan’s version of Interstellar, Matthew McConaughey’s character Cooper was a trained NASA pilot before the events of the film, but NASA had shut down before he could go on any missions. In Spielberg’s version, Cooper is merely a crafty engineer who stumbles upon a space probe returning from deep space. The probe leads him to the secret NASA base where he is then selected for the space mission that’s about to leave Earth.

articles.title: Riot Co-Founder Calls League of Legends MMO the 'Grail' Quest, 5 Years After It Was Announced
articles.summary: League of Legends developer Riot Games is still bashing away on its MMO, which co-founder Mark Merrill recently described as the studio’s “grail quest.” Riot announced its MMO five years ago, in August 2021.
body: “We know what players’ hopes and dreams are,” he said. “It’s just on us as a team, and can we succeed in the execution?”
Merrill said Riot jokingly calls the MMO the “grail” because “f**k it, many a brave knight are gonna die on the grail quest. But f**k it, it’s the grail, so let’s go.”
“That’s the mindset that we really try to cultivate. And that is hard to do at scale,” he continued. “But I think we’re doing a reasonable job. And I think the future’s incredibly bright.”

It’s fair to say Merrill’s comments were met with a healthy dose of skepticism, particularly from fighting game fans. Riot recently announced its League of Legends fighting game, 2XKO, ends active development at the end of this year due to a lack of players. It only released late 2025, so you can understand where this sentiment is coming from.

articles.title: Skytech Gaming Blaze 5 Review
articles.summary: The Skytech Gaming Blaze 5 is packed with strong mid-tier components in a sleek glassy tower, but there are a few issues that’ll impact your quality of life.
body: A custom pre-built gaming PC like the Skytech Gaming Blaze 5 is going to save you a lot of work if you’re not technically savvy or simply don’t have the patience to put together a modern-day puzzle. With its Nvidia GeForce RTX 5070 graphics card and AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D, you’re getting solid mid-tier performance. And it’s all packed away in an easy-to-open glass case with shiny RGB components.

That said, it’s not without issue. Upgrading or replacing components is likely going to take moving a few things out of the way, as it’s a bit crowded on the motherboard. Even if you don’t plan on upgrading, you’ll either be annoyed by the finicky RGB lighting or the fact that the power button and front ports are at the very bottom of the tower, making floor placement very awkward. These may not be dealbreakers for some, but you should know what you’re getting into.
points: The Skytech Gaming Blaze 5 is packed with strong mid-tier components in a sleek glassy tower, but there are a few issues that’ll impact your quality of life.

articles.title: 55 Years Later, Stanley Kubrick's Gritty Sci-Fi Masterpiece Is Officially Back on Streaming
articles.summary: Stanley Kubrick marks a before-and-after in the history of cinema. Few directors have received as much acclaim in life and death, admired by peers and audiences alike.
body: One of his boldest and most uncomfortable movies in a career known for pushing audiences to their limits was A Clockwork Orange. It’s now available on HBO Max.

Based on Anthony Burgess’ novel of the same name, A Clockwork Orange is set in a dystopian near-future Britain, trailing Alex DeLarge (Malcolm McDowell), a terrible young man. As a charming hoodlum speaking in a slang created by Burgess, Alex is instantly memorable, parading through the streets of London with his “droogs” while on the hunt for robbery and rape. Together, they bond as they get drunk, beat up homeless people, and break into strangers’ homes. By day, Alex sleeps in his parents' apartment, skipping school and finding girls to sleep with while the house is empty — rinse and repeat. He’s fully satisfied with his life, feeling no remorse or showing the inklings of a conscience.
points: Stanley Kubrick marks a before-and-after in the history of cinema.
Few directors have received as much acclaim in life and death, admired by peers and audiences alike.

articles.title: BG3's Best Evil Playthrough Replacement Is Waiting to Be Rediscovered on Steam
articles.summary: Baldur’s Gate 3 will absolutely let you be a monster, if you’re so inclined. Slaughter a village, betray every companion, ascend as a vampire tyrant: Do those things, and the game will serve up plenty of deliciously unhinged dialogue options to match.
body: The game doesn’t try to get you to be merciful, but it also doesn’t assist in your malevolence. Betraying an ally you’ve spent hours building trust with doesn’t come with a helpful “this character disapproves” warning light. It just happens, the game informs you of the mess you’ve made, and you’re left with no path forward but to remove your headphones, take your hand off the mouse, and stare at the wall for several minutes, thinking about the enormity of what you’ve just done.
A weekly cheat sheet to what you’ll eventually love to play. No buying, no commitment — just saving for later.

By the end of the game, you’ll need to look at the territories you’ve conquered and decide whether to keep serving Kyros or to turn your armies against the empire that made you. Every move in this game is an ugly power grab, the finale will likely feel odd and unsatisfying — in part because the game was shortened due to budget issues at Obsidian — and since you might not like what you’ve learned about yourself while playing. But you won’t forget the experience anytime soon, either.
points: Baldur’s Gate 3 will absolutely let you be a monster, if you’re so inclined.

articles.title: Dutch artist responds to the White House's Build the Wall game with Build that Bridge
articles.summary: A Dutch artist has released Build that Bridge, a free browser game built as a direct response to Build the Wall, the Tetris-style minigame the White House launched on Arcade.Gov last week.
body: The Trump administration's site includes games inspired by old favourites. For example, Rio Run is a Snake-like game that wants you to collect a chain of prisoners in orange jumpsuits, tallying a "deported" count at the end of each run, and Build the Wall: Zombie Border Siege, a Tetris riff where players stack bricks against incoming "aliens" at the "Southern Border".

Whereas the White House version has players stack blocks into a wall, artist and social designer Wouter Sieuwerts's version, Build that Bridge, uses the same mechanics in reverse: clearing lines grows a bridge from both riverbanks toward the middle.
"Just as the colonisation of America was turned into child's play, the White House now makes a game out of excluding migrants," Sieuwerts said.

"But play is precisely how you discover the world and get to know new people and customs. So for everyone who would rather build bridges than walls, I made Build that Bridge. Play along and make yourself heard."

articles.title: GOTY 2026 is the Weakest Field in Years
articles.summary: It was always going to be a strange year. There was a presumptive winner before the year even began: Grand Theft Auto 6. That remains the case, although, given Rockstar's apparent reticence to let anybody play it, we may be waiting until the eleventh hour for its assumed coronation to be confirmed.
body: Early this year, I kicked off my annual ranking of front-runners for the Game of the Year award at The Game Awards with Resident Evil Requiem in the top spot. It's still there. This is not how I expected things to go. But every potential GOTY contender in 2026 either has huge disadvantages to overcome — because it hails from a genre or franchise that isn't favored — or, quite simply, hasn't been good enough.

It's understandable that this looming behemoth has sucked the air out of the room. But it's still surprising that the race for second place has been so moribund. Quirks of this year's release schedule and slate have been met by a parade of games that have marched up to the quality bar and stopped just short of it — or, perhaps, by a community of game critics that has been less generous than usual with their acclaim.
points: There was a presumptive winner before the year even began: Grand Theft Auto 6.

articles.title: I never thought a fishing sim could be this fun, but How to Fish proves me wrong with its ridiculous physics, killer spider crabs, and classic co-op chaos
articles.summary: I stand knee deep in a pool of blood. My coworkers, comrades, and friends reduced to food for soulless seagulls. Give a man a fish and he may throw it into the mouth of a weary fisherman, teach a man to fish and he shall bring forth the wrath of a spider crab who knows how to stab you with your own…
body: This was my first experience of the new multiplayer fishing sim How to Fish, and now I can see why it's become such a smash-hit among bored and borderline-violent friendship groups.

It has a simple premise: you and up to four friends learn how to fish. The cycle of work involves players buying a basic fishing rod at first, using this to fish for, well, fish and crustaceans, and then beating them to death with your bare knuckles, brass knuckles, or a sick-ass knife. Then you can either eat your catch to replenish your health or hunger or feed it to the lonely fisherman who sits on the dock and gives you coins for your hard work. With the coins gained you can buy more tools to help you fish, like the knife, or supplies which you can use as bait, such as half a hotdog or an empty beer can.
When I first woke up on the island I was met with a friendly punch in the face.

Some things can be so simple that they become boring, and perhaps How to Fish would fall into this trap, if it were just you and the fisherman on the island. But when you add three other people with nothing to lose and access to friendly-fire things get out of hand in the best way possible.

articles.title: Age Twisters is a genuinely charming co-op game hoping to bridge the generation divide - and one of my loveliest surprises at Gamescom
articles.summary: Despite the horrors its name might imply, Age Twisters it's a surprisingly nifty little thing. I had the opportunity to check it out at Gamescom, and to my delight its co-op adventuring provided a lovely tonic to the various violent delights the show provided elsewhere.
body: Developed by Piccolo Studios in Barcelona, Age Twisters - if you're wondering where the name comes from - thrusts two players into the shoes of a grandfather or granddaughter after they receive a strange message from a long-gone mother / daughter. That message arrives with two bracelets enabling the titular age twisting: the ability for our pair to change to various points in their life - child, teenager, adult, elder - at will, each stage providing abilities that can help them solve puzzles.

What follows is a witty adventure that, as you've probably assumed by the premise, is accessible to practically anyone. Piccolo Studios co-founders Jordi Ministral and Alexis Corominas told me the team wanted to make a more cheerful adventure after their last two titles - Arise: A Simple Story and After Us - delved into darker subject matter.

"The story is tied to the generation gap," says Ministral. "Old people being grumpy and greedy, the world is a mess and it's their fault. Young people, lazy snowflakes who don't want to work and complain about everything. All they want to do is drugs and party.
points: Despite the horrors its name might imply, Age Twisters it's a surprisingly nifty little thing.

articles.title: Blending Deus Ex with Escape from Butcher Bay, Deficit is one of the best-feeling indie immersive sims I've played—even if the stealth system needs serious work
articles.summary: Immersive sims like Deus Ex and Dishonored are among the hardest kinds of games to make, so I always try to be supportive when an indie developer takes on the absurd challenge of creating one.
body: Part of the problem is I'm a highly tactile player, and my primary concern when playing any game is whether it feels good beneath the fingers. If a game falls at that initial hurdle, then it's likely (though not inevitable) that I'll drop it pretty quickly. Fortunately, I had the opposite experience with Deficit, an indie imsim with such a strong sense of physicality that I kept playing the demo despite some clear issues.

Developed by Item42, which previously created the cooperative shooter Perish, Deficit sees you play as a freelance spy in a dilapidated, dystopian world. You're tasked with infiltrating a sprawling fortress known as Hadrian's Wall to steal a device called the Interpolator, on behalf of a nameless client known as, well, The Client.

articles.title: Here's 10 more minutes of the most interesting game shown at this year's Opening Night Live
articles.summary: I was largely nonplussed by Gamescom's Opening Night Live, particularly its relentless barrage of identikit fantasy action games that I struggled to tell apart. But one game stood out like a rat-powered computer in an elven glade, and that was Ontos, Frictional Games' latest horror…
body: The Gamescom trailer was a barrage of unsettling, distinctive imagery, from rodent server-racks to slack-jawed dudes with electrodes protruding from their heads. I was instantly intrigued and keen to learn more, so I was delighted to discover that Frictional graced us with a longer look at Ontos in action.

The 10-minute showcase focuses on the same part of the game as the shorter trailer. But it adds significant context to how Ontos plays and the kinds of challenges you'll be dealing with. It starts with the player character—a woman named Aditi—arriving at the hospital wing of Ontos' repurposed 'Moon Hotel' Samsara via an internal railway system, before exploring the wing and unpicking an experiment run by a scientist called Crombie.

articles.title: The Blood of Dawnwalker has sold 1 million copies in just 3 days
articles.summary: The Blood of Dawnwalker, Rebel Wolves' vampire RPG debut, has sold more than a million copies, the studio confirmed on social media.
body: The Blood of Dawnwalker has sold more than a million copies worldwide in just three days.

Developer Rebel Wolves - the studio formed by former Witcher developers - posted the news on Twitter/X over the weekend, writing: "Thank you for playing, sharing, supporting, and being part of the community!"
The Blood of Dawnwalker hit 70,692 concurrents on Steam over the weekend (at the time of writing) - no small feat for a singleplayer game.

After offering a detailed look at the game's console version last week, specifically showing the game wouldn't offer a 60fps mode on PS5 or Xbox Series X/S on launch, the team has since told fans "we heard your feedback", and stressed "it was clear how much this mattered to many of you, so we focused on finishing the next round of tests. Those results gave us the confidence we needed to confirm Performance Mode for Day one ".

articles.title: Civilization 7 will finally enter the atomic age in 2027, via a free update Firaxis says will be 'even bigger in scope' than last year's Test of Time
articles.summary: Despite more than a year of updates and at least one massive overhaul, Civilization 7 remains as stubbornly divisive as ever. May's enormous Test of Time update brought significant mechanical reworks and a fresh influx of players to Firaxis' latest entry in the 4X series.
body: This is partly because numerous aspects of Civ 7 are still rudimentary compared to previous games, including the ability to wage nuclear war While Firaxis' latest allows players to drop atom bombs on their enemies via World War 2 bombers, its final, modern age ends in 1950, meaning many advanced technologies including nuclear submarines and ICBMs are not featured in the game.

Fortunately, this is going to change. Alongside the release of update 1.5.0 —which adds features like improved resource generation and an Earth map where your faction starts at their historically-accurate location—Firaxis outlined its plans for the sequel over the next 12 months. This includes another free update that will finally drag the game into the age of the A-bomb.

The update is called Arc of Tomorrow, and Firaxis says that it will be "even bigger in scope" than May's Test of Time patch. Introducing a fourth Act to Civ 7 that extends the game's timeline from 1950 to 2050, Arc of Tomorrow will bring a host of new features and play opportunities to the experience.
points: Despite more than a year of updates and at least one massive overhaul, Civilization 7 remains as stubbornly divisive as ever.

videos.title: Elden Ring Tarnished Edition - Switch 2 Tech Review - PS4 Visuals With Boosted Res & Frame-Rates
videos.summary: Digital Foundry is now fully independent! Join the DF Supporter Program and support the team:
body: The complete Elden Ring package lands on Switch 2. Visually speaking we're getting a match for the last-gen PS4 release in core settings - though as a plus, Switch 2's frame-rate exceeds that older Sony release, while its resolution locks at the target 1080p more consistently. Comparisons against Series S are less flattering meanwhile. The lack of DLSS is also perhaps a missed opportunity, but on the whole Nintendo's handheld puts in a robust rendition of a true From Software classic.

videos.title: SlashZero - Gameplay Trailer | PS5 Games
videos.summary: SlashZero is a 3D side-scrolling action roguelike game.
body: As a player, you will become a time hacker and be able to traverse across multiple timelines.
Make full use of your action skills and combat strategies, collect items, hunt for clues, piece together the truth, and bring down the final boss!
The feel of the controls, the build configuration, and every aspect of the combat are entirely up to you!
